claims.title: Unipotent exponentials, scalar fixed-cycle blocks, normalized matrix spans, Noetherian coset extraction, and realization assembly
claims.statement: Over a field C of characteristic zero: (1) if a tangent matrix E ∈ M_N(C) of a matrix submonoid S satisfies E² = 0 and every polynomial relation f of S vanishes on the formal exponential exp(s E) in C[[s]], then exp(s E) = I + s E truncates to a linear polynomial and specializing s = 1 places the elementary unipotent matrix I + E in the Zariski closure of S. (2) Let p₀, …, p_(n−1) be pairwise orthogonal nonzero idempotents summing to I_N, let y ∈ M_N(C) permute them via y p_j = p_(π(j)) y, assume y is annihilated by a nonzero polynomial of degree at most n, and suppose y has n distinct eigenvalues λ₀, …, λ_(n−1) with eigenvectors supported on disjoint π-cycles whose spectra do not overlap; then for every fixed point π(i) = i, y acts on the weight space im(p_i) as the pure scalar λ_i (y p_i = λ_i p_i), excluding nontrivial Jordan blocks. (3) If a subalgebra A ⊆ M_N(C) is normalized by a representation ρ : Γ → GL_N(C), then the C-linear span of {a ρ(g) : a ∈ A, g ∈ Γ} is closed under matrix multiplication. (4) For a compact topological group Γ, a matrix representation r : Γ → GL_n(C), and a matrix polynomial f vanishing on a nonempty open subset O ⊆ Γ, the induced Zariski topology on Γ is Noetherian; taking the normal core U of the stabilizer of the irreducible component of 1 yields a finite-index normal subgroup U ⊴ Γ and an element g ∈ Γ such that f(r(g u)) = 0 for all u ∈ U. Together these assemble the key, representation-realization, semisimplicity, matrix-units, and full scalar-corner instances.
claims.hypotheses: Field C (algebraically closed of characteristic zero for the cycle-count and realization theorems), integers N, n ≥ 0, matrix submonoid S ⊆ M_N(C) with formal exponential vanishing on tangent matrices, system of n pairwise orthogonal nonzero idempotents summing to I_N permuted by y with disjoint cycle spectra and an annihilating polynomial of degree at most n, compact topological group Γ with matrix representation ρ or r, and linear polynomial pullback (chain rule) for left matrix translation.
claims.correspondence: Nilpotence E² = 0 forces the formal exponential series to terminate at degree one so polynomial vanishing in C[[s]] evaluates at s = 1. Exhausting the n distinct eigenvalues of a degree-bounded operator forces P(y) = ∏_j (y − λ_j I) = 0, and inductively stripping every factor j ≠ i on im(p_i) using disjoint cycle spectra forces y p_i = λ_i p_i. Normality ρ(g) A ρ(g⁻¹) ⊆ A rewrites products of generators inside the span, while compactness plus Noetherianity of Spec(C[X_(i,j)]) turns an open vanishing locus into a finite-index normal coset via the stabilizer of the identity component.

claims.title: Linear polynomial chain rule, invariant tangent derivations, Lagrange spectral projectors, and lacunary Lie-algebra structure
claims.statement: Let C be a field and N, M, n ≥ 0 integers. (1) For every C-linear map φ : M_N(C) → M_M(C) and matrix polynomial f ∈ C[X_(i,j)] (on M × M entries), substituting the linear coordinate forms of φ produces a polynomial f' on M_N(C) satisfying f'(x) = f(φ(x)) and the directional-derivative chain rule d(f', x, Y) = d(f, φ(x), φ(Y)) for all x, Y ∈ M_N(C). (2) For any matrix submonoid S ⊆ M_N(C) and Y ∈ M_N(C), the right-invariant derivation D_Y satisfies (D_Y f)(x) = d(f, x, Y x); hence Y lies in the Zariski tangent space of S at the identity if and only if D_Y preserves the vanishing ideal of S. (3) If X ∈ M_N(C) is annihilated by a nonzero polynomial of degree at most n and has n distinct eigenvalues e₀, …, e_(n−1) ∈ C, then its minimal polynomial equals ∏_(k=0)^(n−1) (T − e_k), and evaluating the Lagrange interpolation polynomials b_i(T) = ∏_(j≠i) (T − e_j)/(e_i − e_j) at X yields pairwise orthogonal nonzero idempotents p_i = b_i(X) ∈ C[X] with ∑_i p_i = I_N and X = ∑_i e_i p_i; moreover, every eigenvector y v = μ v satisfies Q(y) v = Q(μ) v for all Q ∈ C[T]. (4) Combined with the lacunary-weight condition (disjoint nonempty subsets A, B ⊆ {0, …, n−1} satisfy |B| ∑_(i∈A) e_i ≠ |A| ∑_(j∈B) e_j) and specialization to the algebraically closed coefficient field K, these assemble the Lie-spectrum, global degree-bound, and full tangent-algebra structure theorems.
claims.hypotheses: Field C (and algebraically closed extension K'/K of characteristic zero for specialization and lacunary Lie-algebra data), integers N, M, n ≥ 0, C-linear map φ : M_N(C) → M_M(C), matrix submonoid S ⊆ M_N(C), matrix X ∈ M_N(C) with an annihilator of degree at most n and n distinct eigenvalues e₀, …, e_(n−1), and compact topological group Γ with continuous semisimple representation ρ : Γ → GL_N(K).
claims.correspondence: Structural induction on multivariate polynomials using the Leibniz rule establishes the linear chain rule and identifies right-invariant derivations D_Y with directional derivatives along Y x, equating tangency at I with ideal preservation. Coprime linear factors of distinct eigenvalues force the minimal polynomial of a degree-n matrix to be ∏(T − e_k), so Lagrange interpolation constructs the exact orthogonal spectral projector system and wires the full tangent-algebra structure assembly.

claims.title: Zariski multiplicative closure, semisimple reverse embedding, characteristic-polynomial matching, and unconditional rank-extraction assembly
claims.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and Γ a compact topological group. (1) For any matrix submonoid S ⊆ M_N(K), two-stage linear pullback along left multiplication by s ∈ S and right multiplication by y in the Zariski closure S̄ shows that S̄ is closed under matrix multiplication. (2) Given continuous semisimple ρ : Γ → GL_N(K), a representation r : Γ → GL_n(K) with an intertwiner A ∈ M_(N×n)(K), linear left inverse B (B A = I_n), and the spanning condition (every Z ∈ M_N(K) killing all intertwiners r → ρ vanishes), semisimplicity descends from ρ to r, rank(A) = n, r(g) = B ρ(g) A, and for every g ∈ Γ and q ∈ K[T] one has q(ρ(g)) = 0 if and only if q(r(g)) = 0. (3) If x ∈ M_n(K) is annihilated by a monic degree-n polynomial P ∈ K[T], then every eigenvalue of x lies in the root set of P; hence the characteristic polynomial χ_x equals P whenever either χ_x is separable, or P is product-generic (no distinct degree-n multiset of roots of P has the same product) and det(x) = (−1)^n P(0). (4) By finite-dimensional descent on dim ker E for equivariant idempotents E in the span of rank factorizations t' ∘ t through r, the identity I_N writes as ∑_(j=1)^k t'_j t_j with equivariant t_j : ρ → r and t'_j : r → ρ, embedding ρ ↪ r^(⊕k). (5) Assembling all thirteen verified instances discharges the lacunary rank-extraction theorem unconditionally, yielding continuous semisimple r : Γ → GL_n(K) with r ↪ ρ, ρ ↪ r^(⊕k), det(r) = ψ, open dense separable-spectrum locus, and χ_(r(s)) = P_s on separable and product-generic points.
claims.hypotheses: Compact topological group Γ, algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero with algebraically closed extension K'/K, continuous semisimple matrix representation ρ : Γ → GL_N(K), dense subset S ⊆ Γ with monic degree-n polynomials P_s annihilating ρ(s), continuous character ψ : Γ → K^× matching (−1)^n P_s(0) on S, and a Zariski Lie-algebra matrix X ∈ M_N(K') possessing n distinct lacunary eigenvalues.
claims.correspondence: Two-stage polynomial pullback closes S̄ under multiplication; pulling invariant complements back along an injective intertwiner A transfers semisimplicity and polynomial annihilation; multiset cardinality and Vieta sign (−1)^(2n) = 1 prove characteristic-polynomial matching under separability or product-genericity; equivariant idempotent ascent splits ker E one nonvanishing intertwiner at a time to reach I_N = ∑ t'_j t_j, completing all thirteen components of the unconditional lacunary rank-extraction assembly.
